biography: Lewis Williamson, born in the Scottish Highlands, wasn't raised in a racing family. His father was a shepherd, and Lewis spent his early years tending to the flock amidst the rugged terrain. His racing journey began unexpectedly when a local rally team needed a mechanic's assistant. Lewis, eager to escape the farm, took the job. He soon showed an uncanny aptitude for understanding the machines, and then, during a test day, the driver fell ill. Lewis, despite never having raced, was given a chance. He shocked everyone, including himself, with his natural talent. A defining moment came in his first season in Formula Ford; down two laps due to an early spin, he clawed his way back to win, showcasing his relentless spirit. Now, at 35, Williamson finds himself as a veteran presence at Trophy Mira Orange, mentoring young drivers while still chasing his own ambitions of a championship title.
drivingStyle: Williamson's driving style is marked by a steady hand and an analytical approach. He isn't the most flamboyant driver, preferring to build momentum throughout a race. He excels at tire management, often nursing his rubber to gain an advantage in the later stages. He rarely makes rash decisions, preferring a calculated risk assessment before attempting an overtake. Under pressure, Williamson remains remarkably composed, a trait honed from years of experience and a quiet confidence in his abilities.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision that cost Alvarez the championship in 2020. Alvarez believes Williamson deliberately took him out.
A new rivalry brewing due to consistent on-track battles and similar driving styles. Their fights for position are always intense and strategic.

Tanaka and Williamson have been rivals since Formula 3, where they traded wins and close finishes. Their rivalry is based on mutual respect, but both are desperate to prove themselves the better driver.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky blue socks on race days, regardless of the weather.
Spends 15 minutes meditating in his race car before every session.
Refuses to eat anything green on race weekends.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about raw speed; it's about understanding the rhythm of the machine and finding harmony with the track."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2018, co-driving a privately-entered prototype. The victory was a shock to the established factory teams and cemented Williamson's reputation as a driver who could deliver under pressure.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Spa 24 Hours in 2021. A mechanical failure was to blame, but the disappointment lingered for months, making him question his future in racing.
